title: Page transition for the complexity of an evaporating black hole
authors: Violet Concepcion, Yasunori Nomura, Kyle Ritchie, Samuel Weiss
abstract: Recent results demonstrate that there exists a sharp, Page-like transition for the complexity of subsystems of Haar-random states as their fractional subsystem size surpasses one half. They further demonstrate that this transition also occurs for the holographic complexity of boundary subregions of eternal AdS black holes, assuming the Complexity$=$Volume (CV) proposal for subregions. We interpret this transition as a crossover from spectrum-dominated to basis-dominated subsystem complexity, reflecting the breakdown of approximate thermality beyond half-system size. We then apply this reasoning to an evaporating AdS black hole coupled to a bath, modeled by a quantum circuit undergoing random evolution on an interior subsystem of diminishing size. Using the basis-spectrum decomposition of subsystem complexity, we argue for a similar Page-like transition in the radiation complexity. We then show, using CV for subregions, that the same transition appears in the holographic complexity of the radiation subsystem through the emergence of an island, whose volume gives the dominant contribution. We argue that the island volume contribution resolves an apparent complexity paradox analogous to the information paradox.
summary: This theoretical work applies concepts from quantum complexity theory to black hole evaporation within the AdS/CFT framework. It predicts that holographic complexity exhibits a Page-like transition when the radiation subsystem grows past half its size. This transition is attributed to an 'island' region, suggesting this mechanism resolves a deep paradox analogous to the information loss problem.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether a Page-like transition occurs for the holographic complexity of subsystems during black hole evaporation, analogous to the resolution of the information paradox.
main_result: A Page-like transition is predicted in the radiation complexity due to the emergence of an 'island' contribution when using the Complexity=Volume (CV) proposal, which resolves a complexity paradox similar to the information paradox.
method: The authors employ quantum information tools like basis-spectrum decomposition and holographic complexity calculations, comparing them against circuit models for subsystem complexity.
model_or_system: The system modeled is an evaporating Anti-de Sitter (AdS) black hole coupled to a bath, analyzed using concepts from AdS/CFT correspondence and quantum circuits representing the interior dynamics.
key_observables: Subsystem complexity (general and holographic), radiation complexity, and the volume contribution of the 'island' region.
important_parameters: The subsystem size relative to half ($	ext{size} > 1/2$), and the time evolution across the Page time.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Complexity=Volume (CV) proposal for subregions, and models black hole evaporation via random circuit evolution on an interior subsystem.
figures_summary: Figures sketch maximal volume slices in AdS/Schwarzschild diagrams showing how the island forms post-Page time, causing a dramatic change in the calculated volume contribution.
paper_structure: The paper builds from established results on complexity transitions for random states to applying these concepts to the holographic complexity of an evaporating black hole, culminating in the prediction and interpretation of the Page-like transition via the island structure.
why_interesting: While focused on gravity/QFT, the core methodology—analyzing how information measures (complexity) undergo sharp transitions based on subsystem size relative to a critical point—is highly relevant to understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1: (a) We sketch the maximal volume slices associated with the boundary at a given time in the AdS/Schwarzschild Penrose diagram. Before the Page time, we have the light red slices which go through the interior of the black hole. The blue slices end on the edge of the island, since they are the maximal volume slices through the entanglement wedge of the CFT living on the boundary, which no longer includes the island. At late times, the dark blue slices represent the post-black hole near-flat maximal volume slices. (b) We depict the value of the volume qualitatively. It increases at a rate proportional to M 2 until the time the island forms, at which point the volume drops...

Figure 2: Before the Page time tPage, the entanglement wedge e(R) of the bath system is the bath itself. The entanglement wedge e(B) of the CFT (living on the AdS bound- ary) at time t1 < tPage is the region in AdSd that can be reached from the equal-time hypersurface of the boundary at t1.

Figure 3: After the Page time, the bath’s entanglement wedge (pink) now includes the black hole interior. The entanglement wedge of the CFT degrees of freedom (blue) extends to the black hole exterior.
Figure 4: A time dependent quantum circuit as a set of N qubits. Every ∆t we act on the circuit with an operator H which consists of a product of p-gates, acting nonlocally.

Figure 5: A time dependent quantum circuit that more closely resembles a system undergoing evaporation. Since the black hole is a fast scrambler, we see rapid interac- tions modeled such that an operator H consisting of a product of p-gates acts on the circuit in every time interval ∆t. We also have a bath system in which no interactions occur, and no gates are used. Every ∆t we remove one qubit from the circuit to this bath system.
